resources.string: Honest video recovery: finds what your phone can still reach, and tells you clearly what is gone.
Scans every video Android can still see, including items in the system trash (Android 11+), which can be restored.
Read-only scan of a folder or SD card: hidden videos, .trashed files, unlabeled video files and leftover thumbnails.
Checks whether recovery is technically possible and walks you through every outside place your videos may still exist.
Works fully offline. No internet permission. Nothing is uploaded or shared. Scans are read-only: original files are never changed, moved or deleted.

Modern Android phones encrypt storage. Once a video is permanently deleted and its space reused, or the phone is factory reset, no app can bring it back. This app never shows fake results or recovery percentages.

Lists videos Android still exposes. Items marked TRASH are in the system Recently Deleted area and can be restored. Note: some gallery apps (for example Samsung Gallery) keep their own private bin that other apps cannot read; check it inside that gallery app. A listed normal video is a video that still exists, not a recovered deleted file.

Choose your SD card (or any folder). The scan only reads files. It finds hidden videos, .trashed files, videos without a name extension (checked by file signature) and leftover .thumbnails. Truly erased videos need a raw scan on a computer; tap the PC guide.
Nothing found here. This does not prove the video is gone forever; check the outside sources in Factory Reset Assessment.
Permission denied. The app needs video access to scan. You can allow it from phone Settings → Apps → Nexus Deep Recovery AI → Permissions.
THUMBNAIL ONLY (small picture, not the video)
Copying… original file is not changed.
Copy cancelled. The partial copy was removed.
Restored. The video is back in your gallery.
No app on this phone can open this file.

Android does not let apps read the raw sectors of an SD card, so erased videos cannot be carved from the phone. Free, safe method:

1. Stop using the SD card immediately. Do not take new photos or videos on it.
2. Take it out and put it in a card reader on a Windows, Mac or Linux computer.
3. Download PhotoRec (free and open source, part of TestDisk by CGSecurity) from cgsecurity.org.
4. Select the SD card, choose the "Free" space option, and in File Opt keep mov / mp4 / 3gp / mkv selected.
5. Save the output to the computer's own drive, never to the SD card.
6. Open the recovered folder and check the videos.

Note: this works only on SD cards and old unencrypted storage. It does not work on a modern phone's internal memory.
⚠ Run this check on the phone that lost the videos. Use that phone as little as possible: every new photo, app update or download can overwrite old data.

Storage encryption: ON.

After a factory reset, the encryption key is destroyed. The old internal data becomes random noise that no app, AI or lab can read. Videos deleted a long time ago have also usually been overwritten.

Result: internal recovery is not possible. Your real chance is the outside sources below.

Storage encryption: OFF or not supported (usually very old phones).\n\nIn theory a professional forensic lab might recover some data, but it needs root access or opening the phone, and is not possible from an app. Stop using the phone and check the outside sources below first.
Storage encryption status could not be read. Android 10 and newer phones are always encrypted, so treat internal recovery after a factory reset as not possible. Check the outside sources below.
Where your videos may still exist
Check Library → Trash (kept 60 days), Archive and Locked Folder. Also log in with every other Gmail you ever used on the old phone.
Download everything stored in a Google account and search it for videos.
See device and WhatsApp backups and their sizes.
Anyone you sent a video to may still have it. Ask them: open the chat → tap the name → Media, links and docs → forward it back.
Download your information from Accounts Centre; it includes uploaded and archived videos, stories and reels.
Videos you uploaded (even private or draft) can be downloaded from YouTube Studio or TikTok settings.
Samsung and some other phones sync the gallery to OneDrive or the maker\'s cloud.
Old phone, SD card or computer
Check any old phone, memory card, laptop or USB where you may have copied videos. Use the SD Card section to scan them.

Checks every file and folder on the phone and SD card: phone-maker gallery Recycle Bins (Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, Huawei), trash, WhatsApp / Telegram / Instagram / TikTok media and cache, renamed videos, and pictures of old deleted videos left in thumbnail caches. Shows which app each video came from and whether it plays.

Reads every file on internal storage and any SD card, one by one, and checks file signatures. It finds every video file that still physically exists, even if hidden, renamed or left in an app cache. It cannot rebuild videos Android has already erased or that were lost in a factory reset, because that storage is encrypted. Needs "All files access". Read-only: nothing is changed.
Deep scan needs \"All files access\". On the next screen turn ON \"Allow access to manage all files\" for Nexus Deep Recovery AI, then come back.
Repair / rebuild video (saves a new copy)
Rebuilding the video into a fresh MP4… the original is not changed.

This video cannot be rebuilt: its index (moov) is missing, so Android cannot read its frames. Try copying it anyway; a PC tool such as untrunc (free) with a healthy video from the same phone can sometimes fix it.
